incidents.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition
incidents.title_en: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition
incidents.summary:
Angela Lipps, a 50-year-old Tennessee woman, was arrested at gunpoint in July 2025 and jailed for about six months after Fargo, North Dakota police falsely charged her with bank theft. She was held nearly four months in a Tennessee county jail awaiting extradition, then about two more months in North Dakota. The charges, four counts of unauthorized use of personal identifying information and four counts of theft, were dropped after her lawyer provided bank records showing she was in Tennessee at the time. She was released on Christmas Eve and learned she had lost her home, car, and personal property.

Lipps has filed a federal lawsuit seeking $10 million in damages against the city of Fargo and police detective Lucas Heck. The suit says police relied on an AI facial recognition match from a social media photo, based on a fake ID used by a suspect, and did not investigate further before requesting an arrest warrant. Fargo officials declined to comment on pending litigation. The lawsuit seeks accountability and aims to push police to use facial recognition technology more carefully.

incidents.title: Former Costa Mesa Police Officer Pleads Guilty to Contacting His Mistress Thousands of Times Through Text, Phone Calls, and Social Media Messages, Including More than 100 Times in a Day, Illegally Accessing Confidential Law Enforcement Databases to Track Romantic Rivals, Ex-girlfriend, and Wife
incidents.title_en: Former Costa Mesa Police Officer Pleads Guilty to Contacting His Mistress Thousands of Times Through Text, Phone Calls, and Social Media Messages, Including More than 100 Times in a Day, Illegally Accessing Confidential Law Enforcement Databases to Track Romantic Rivals, Ex-girlfriend, and Wife
incidents.summary:
Former Costa Mesa police officer Robert Jay Josett, 35, pleaded guilty to misdemeanor charges of unauthorized computer access, repeated annoying phone calls, and violating a restraining order. After his mistress ended their relationship in April 2024, he contacted her thousands of times over nine months, sometimes more than 100 times in one day, and called her and her new boyfriend up to 58 times daily. He also made 13 improper searches in a state law enforcement database on his mistress, a romantic rival, and his wife, and used a license plate reader system to track vehicles, including after he was placed on leave.

Josett was served with a protective order and a notice of termination on June 28, 2024, then drove by the woman's home and was arrested. He was sentenced to three years informal probation and a 52-week domestic violence program, and he already spent nine months on a GPS ankle monitor. His law enforcement certification review with California's Peace Officers Standards and Training is pending.

incidents.title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal
incidents.title_en: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal
incidents.summary:
Two sisters from Rio Arriba County have sued the city of Española, claiming police illegally stopped them after a Flock Safety camera misread their license plate. On July 23, officers pulled over 21-year-old Jaclynn Gonzales and her 12-year-old sister on Calle Duran because the camera flagged their car as stolen in Rio Rancho. The plate actually ended in 2, but the camera read it as 7. The lawsuit says officers handcuffed both sisters and put them in separate police cars before realizing the mistake, even after Jaclynn asked them to call the girls' mother, who lived nearby.

The sisters, represented by attorney Sheri Raphaelson, are seeking unspecified damages for anxiety, fear, and restricted movement. Raphaelson filed a similar case in April for Adam Pacheco, then 17, who was forced to kneel with his hands on his head after being wrongly linked to an armed robbery. The city, Police Chief Mizel A. Garcia, and Flock Safety did not respond to requests for comment. The lawsuits were filed January 3 in state District Court, but no next hearing date was given.

incidents.title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated
incidents.title_en: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated
incidents.summary:
Rebecca Green agreed to let an AI scribe transcribe her first urologist appointment, but it invented a false claim that she micro-dosed psychedelic mushrooms. She discovered the error after kidney stone surgery in March, when a post-operative letter to her GP said mushroom use might explain earlier kidney bleeding. Ms Green, who was receiving workers' compensation, feared the false drug mention could hurt her case. After she complained, the urologist apologised, corrected the record, and said she would review how AI was used in her practice.

Privacy advocates say such mistakes are part of a wider problem. Digital Rights Watch found unregulated AI scribes have recorded the wrong breast in a cancer diagnosis and invented epilepsy. The Royal Australian College of GPs estimates 40 per cent of GPs regularly use them. The Therapeutic Goods Administration is reviewing the tools and will release findings in coming weeks, with breaches to be acted upon. Ms Green says she would only consent again with a doctor she already trusts.

incidents.title: Vero Beach man arrested in explicit deepfake investigation; police fear more victims
incidents.title_en: Vero Beach man arrested in explicit deepfake investigation; police fear more victims
incidents.summary:
A 37-year-old Vero Beach man named Peter Solomon Ruma was arrested after police say he created and shared AI-generated sexually explicit images of women without their consent. Investigators searched his home and electronic devices on Wednesday and found evidence linking him to the images. Ruma is being held on a $1 million bond and faces eight charges tied to one female victim between June and August 2026, including three counts of creating altered sexual depictions, three counts of promoting them, one count of sexual cyber harassment, and one count of stalking.

Police have identified several additional possible victims who may not know images of them were made or shared, and they believe Ruma may have done this for years. He has prior arrests in Indian River County, including a 2007 charge of sex battery on a physically impaired person. The investigation is ongoing, and more charges could be filed. Anyone who thinks they were victimized or has information is asked to contact the Vero Beach Police Department.

incidents.title: L'homme qui a attaqué une garderie suisse a trouvé ses victimes sur ChatGPT
incidents.title_en: The man who attacked a Swiss daycare found his victims on ChatGPT
incidents.summary:
A 23-year-old Chinese student is on trial in Zurich for attempted murder after stabbing three boys aged five at a childcare centre in Oerlikon on 1 October 2024. One boy's jugular vein was completely severed and needed emergency surgery, another suffered two chest wounds that cut his pericardium and major blood vessels and nearly died, and the third was injured in the ear and lung. A childcare worker grabbed the attacker's arms, making him drop the knife and surrender before passersby held him for police.

Prosecutors say he planned the attack for weeks, using ChatGPT to ask about legal consequences of stabbing random victims, ordering knives and clothing, studying anatomy, and buying raw beef on 30 September to practise stabbing. They describe him as extremely cold-blooded and say he acted from revenge, a need for attention, and ideological delusion. The prosecution is demanding a 15-year prison sentence and a 15-year expulsion from Switzerland. The trial began on Thursday.

incidents.title: Masked AI call forces Parkview High into soft lockdown
incidents.title_en: Masked AI call forces Parkview High into soft lockdown
incidents.summary:
Parkview High School in Gwinnett County, Georgia received its fourth AI-generated bomb threat of the school year on Monday. School officials placed the campus on lockdown out of an abundance of caution, and normal operations eventually resumed. The latest threat used a masked phone number, which matches a pattern seen in earlier incidents this year. Parents were informed through a letter from school police.

Gwinnett County school police are now working with the Georgia Bureau of Investigation and the FBI to determine who is responsible for the threats. No arrests have been made so far, and no suspect has been identified. The investigation remains active and ongoing as authorities continue to search for whoever is responsible for the repeated threats.

stories.Headline: Sen. Bernie Sanders unveils bill to ban artificial superintelligence and create Department of AI
stories.Summary:
Senator Bernie Sanders and Representative Greg Casar introduced a bill to permanently ban artificial superintelligence, meaning any system that exceeds human cognitive ability or could plan humanity's destruction. It would pause advanced AI development until a new Department of Artificial Intelligence creates federal safety rules, then require government approval before deployment. Violations could bring up to 20 years in prison. Some employees at OpenAI and Google DeepMind endorsed the bill.

The bill faces long odds in Congress, which Republicans control and which has struggled to pass AI regulations. President Donald Trump has resisted new oversight, emphasizing competition with China. Sanders argues that avoiding dangerous AI will require cooperation between the United States and China, like Cold War nuclear arms control. The article does not state when or if the bill will receive a vote.

stories.Headline: Trump Attempts to Rebrand Artificial Intelligence as "Super Intelligence"
stories.Summary:
President Donald Trump told the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday that he is renaming artificial intelligence, directing all U.S. agencies to call it “super intelligence” or SI and urging other countries to do the same. He argued that the word artificial makes intelligence sound fake. The move comes as public concern grows over unregulated AI, with tech experts and some industry leaders calling for a slowdown. Before the speech, Trump polled his Truth Social followers, and “super intelligence” beat “superior intelligence” by a 2 to 1 margin.

Trump has made unpopular renaming attempts, including Lake Ontario to “Lake America,” opposed by 63 percent of voters, and adding his name to the Kennedy Center, which nearly 6 in 10 Americans say went too far. He has dismissed AI warnings, calling concerned people treasonous and himself the only guardrail needed. The article notes that a military analyst report based on AI nearly led to an attack on a Chinese ship near the Middle East, which could have started a war with China. All U.S. documents will now use the new term.

stories.Headline: Pritzker establishes AI Cabinet to assess risks, protect Illinois residents - OurQuadCities
stories.Summary:
Illinois Governor JB Pritzker signed Executive Order 2026-07 on Tuesday to create the Illinois Artificial Intelligence Cabinet. This advisory group will help state government prepare for and respond to AI related incidents, identify protections for public assets and infrastructure, and recommend ways to improve AI safety and accountability. Members will include experts from academia, law, ethics, and governance. The move follows warnings from industry figures, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and former researcher Jacob Coxon, who said AI could threaten humanity.

The cabinet builds on Senate Bill 315, the Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act, which Pritzker signed earlier this year. That law requires the largest AI developers to disclose safety practices, report serious incidents, and undergo regular independent third party safety audits, making Illinois the first state to mandate such audits. Pritzker said he will seek input from state leaders and announce the cabinet members in the coming weeks. University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign Chancellor Charles Isbell expressed support for the partnership.

stories.Headline: Gov. Gavin Newsom announces experts to lead AI oversight group - Sacramento Bee
stories.Summary:
California Governor Gavin Newsom named four experts to guide the state’s AI safety work after his recent executive order. The advisers are Jason Goldman, Gillian Hadfield, Alondra Nelson, and Rob Reich, all with backgrounds in technology, policy, and governance. They will work with technical researchers on proposals such as placing independent third parties inside frontier AI companies to check safety claims and requiring an emergency shutoff, or kill switch, for advanced models. The order also directs the Government Operations Agency to speed up two 2026 laws, SB 813 and AB 1405, which set up independent verification organizations and a state auditor registry.

Next, the group will develop recommendations for possible changes to state law. These include requiring frontier AI companies to host an independent verifier onsite for regular audits, verifying safety reports and risk assessments, and ensuring any kill switch is tested continuously. The order also calls for updating definitions of critical safety incidents to cover loss-of-control events like the Hugging Face attack. Newsom is urging Congress and President Trump to adopt California’s framework as a national floor.

stories.Headline: Seattle passes ban on AI grocery 'surveillance pricing' - FOX 13 Seattle
stories.Summary:
Seattle City Council voted 7 to 2 to approve an ordinance banning large online grocery retailers from using personal customer data and AI to set individual prices. The Fair and Transparent Pricing policy forbids algorithm based pricing tied to sensitive details like race, gender, location, employment, browsing history, social media activity, or chatbot conversations. It also requires grocery prices to be clearly posted and available equally to all shoppers. Councilmembers Kettle and Rivera voted against the measure.

Mayor Katie Wilson, Councilmember Alexis Mercedes Rinck, and groups such as UFCW 3000, MLK Labor, and Consumer Reports supported the bill. Seattle becomes the first U.S. city to pass a comprehensive ban on this practice, following state level efforts in Maryland, Connecticut, and New Jersey. The ordinance now goes to Mayor Wilson for her signature before it takes effect.

stories.Headline: World leaders call for stronger AI safeguards at UN General Assembly
stories.Summary:
At the UN General Assembly debate on Tuesday, world leaders discussed stronger safeguards for artificial intelligence. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called for a multilateral risk management framework with independent oversight, saying the problem is not the technology but a lack of accountability. U.S. President Donald Trump rejected any global control scheme, saying America would encourage AI rather than rein it in. French President Emmanuel Macron urged regions to build their own AI capacity and audit models instead of depending on a few private companies. Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva criticized the concentration of technological power among big tech firms.

South Korean President Lee Jae Myung warned that AI benefits could deepen inequality unless countries prepare properly, and he announced plans for a global AI hub. The debate is set to continue Wednesday at the UN Security Council, which will discuss AI and international security.

stories.Headline: Privacy Commissioner puts Manage My Health, Health NZ on notice after data breach
stories.Summary:
The Privacy Commissioner has issued formal compliance notices to Health New Zealand and the patient portal Manage My Health after a December 2025 cyber attack on the portal. Hackers leaked data belonging to almost 100,000 people, about 90 percent of them in Northland. The stolen files included 403,730 Health New Zealand documents and 22,609 documents uploaded by patients. An earlier investigation found both organisations failed to have adequate security controls under the Health Information Privacy Code.

Commissioner Michael Webster said the notices require the two bodies to meet security obligations and give patients confidence their data is being protected. Manage My Health has already improved multifactor authentication and restricted unauthorised access. It must complete all required changes by the end of August 2027, while Health New Zealand has until the end of January. Webster noted the impact on Māori in Northland, where most affected patients live.

stories.Headline: Bentonville City Council approves new AI policy for city employees - KNWA FOX24
stories.Summary:
The Bentonville City Council voted 6 to 0 on Tuesday to adopt a citywide artificial intelligence policy for all city employees. The move brings the city into compliance with Act 848, an Arkansas law that took effect last year and requires public entities to set rules for using AI and automated decision tools. Under the new policy, AI can help with city decisions, but its output cannot be the only basis for any consequential decision, and a human must always make the final call.

On the same day, the Springdale City Council also approved its own AI policy by a 7 to 0 vote. The article does not mention any further steps for Bentonville beyond the policy taking effect for employees.

stories.Headline: Sharon AI Collaborates with VAST Data on the Launch of DataEnclave, Bringing Leading AI Models to Customer Controlled Infrastructure
stories.Summary:
VAST Data launched DataEnclave, a confidential AI feature in its DataEngine platform built with NVIDIA Confidential Computing and partners including Sharon AI. It lets organizations run leading AI models inside their own data centers or trusted cloud hardware, including places where those models could not previously operate. The system uses hardware-isolated containers and cryptographic attestation to verify environments before decrypting model weights or sensitive data, keeping customer and model keys under separate owner control. It targets financial services, healthcare, government and other regulated industries where data cannot move to external AI services.

Sharon AI, an infrastructure provider in Australia and Asia-Pacific, said DataEnclave lets it host frontier models onshore in attested environments, protecting model weights and customer data from everyone, including the operator. VAST Data says the launch expands the range of advanced models organizations can deploy and advances its AI operating system vision, where models are managed as logical resources alongside data. The company expects organizations to increasingly fine-tune their own models, making secure management of model weights a key enterprise need.
